# Default parameter values

<!-- Generated by tools/assumptions/check.py --render from assumptions/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every value below is a default in Project Preferences → Parameters (ADR-0018) and can be changed per project.
**Basis** says where the value comes from: `cited` (a named clause or table), `documented` (derived from
documented values, derivation in the rationale) or `educated-guess` (no source found; reasoning written down,
deliberately wide range). **Check** says how far a maintainer has verified it: `read` (clause read),
`secondary` (confirmed through a source quoting it) or `unverified` (clause reference given but not yet read
against the current text; please confirm before relying on it).

Schema and contribution rules: [README.md](README.md).

## Modes

### Curve radius, minimum

`mode.min_curve_radius_m` · unit: m · used by: alignment check (error below this), swept-path check, vehicle–infrastructure compatibility

| Context | Low | Central | High | Basis | Check | Sources | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | 12.5 | 25 | 300 | educated-guess | unverified | [mobsimlab-derivation](#src-mobsimlab-derivation) | Wide fallback spanning road vehicles to mainline rail; every mode below has its own entry. |
| bus, brt, trolleybus, intercity_bus | 12.5 | 12.5 | 12.5 | cited | unverified | [eu-dir-96-53](#src-eu-dir-96-53) | Directive 96/53/EC Annex I 1.5: a road vehicle must turn within a circle of 12.5 m outer radius (5.3 m inner). Used as the outer swept radius at walking pace, not as a running radius. |
| tram | 15 | 20 | 25 | documented | secondary | [tud-tram-radius](#src-tud-tram-radius), [bostrab](#src-bostrab) | Practice in German networks is about 20 to 30 m with extremes just under 12 m (seminar slides); BOStrab §17(3) only requires radii on segregated track to avoid speed restrictions. Depot tracks can go lower; vehicle file wins. |
| light_rail | 20 | 25 | 50 | documented | unverified | [tud-tram-radius](#src-tud-tram-radius), [bostrab-trr](#src-bostrab-trr) | Light rail vehicles still run street sections, so the tram minimum applies at junctions; segregated sections use the recommended radius. |
| metro | 60 | 100 | 150 | educated-guess | unverified | [mobsimlab-derivation](#src-mobsimlab-derivation) | Metro stock is typically specified for about 60 to 100 m on running lines (lower in depots). Wide range; take the vehicle file value when it exists. |
| commuter_rail | 150 | 300 | 600 | documented | unverified | [en-13803](#src-en-13803), [mobsimlab-derivation](#src-mobsimlab-derivation) | Derived from R = 11.8 v² / (D + I) with v = 120 km/h, D = 160 mm cant, I = 130 mm cant deficiency gives about 590 m for full line speed; 150–300 m is what mainline EMUs accept at reduced speed. |
| regional_rail | 300 | 600 | 1050 | documented | unverified | [en-13803](#src-en-13803), [mobsimlab-derivation](#src-mobsimlab-derivation) | R = 11.8 v² / (D + I): v = 160 km/h, D = 160, I = 130 gives about 1040 m; lower values impose a local speed restriction. |
| long_distance_rail | 600 | 1050 | 1650 | documented | unverified | [en-13803](#src-en-13803), [mobsimlab-derivation](#src-mobsimlab-derivation) | R = 11.8 v² / (D + I): v = 160 km/h → about 1040 m; v = 200 km/h → about 1630 m. |
| high_speed_rail | 2240 | 3220 | 4380 | documented | unverified | [en-13803](#src-en-13803), [eu-reco-2001-290](#src-eu-reco-2001-290), [mobsimlab-derivation](#src-mobsimlab-derivation) | R = 11.8 v² / (D + I) with D = 180 mm (2001/290/EC limit for new high-speed lines) and I = 150 mm: v = 250 km/h → about 2240 m (low), 300 km/h → about 3220 m (central), 350 km/h → about 4380 m (high). |

## Energy supply systems

Vehicles list the supply systems they support (`supplySystems`); a section can only be run by a vehicle
whose list contains the section's system, whose pantograph head or collector shoe fits the listed options,
and whose voltage range covers Umin1–Umax1. Central values; where options exist the central value is the
default and the others are accepted. Full basis, sources and rationale per attribute:
[`supply-systems.yaml`](supply-systems.yaml).
